svg.title: How to read the DePriester chart (K values of light hydrocarbons)
svg.text: How to read the DePriester chart (K values of light hydrocarbons)
High-temperature DePriester chart (nomograph), redrawn from Wankat Eq. 2-30 / Table 2-3
Find the pressure on the left scale (here p = 400 kPa).
Find the temperature on the right scale (here T = 60 °C).
Join the two points with a ruler (one straight line).
Where the ruler crosses a component scale, read that K (propane 4.24, n-butane 1.60, n-hexane 0.243).
Reverse use: a line through a known K and p (or T) gives the other variable, e.g. bubble/dew points.
Use the low-temperature chart below 20 °C (−70 to 20 °C) and the high-temperature chart above.
Redrawn from the correlation; in the exam read the printed chart — values may differ slightly.
